configurePresets.name: base
configurePresets.description: Shared settings. VCPKG_ROOT must point at a bootstrapped vcpkg checkout; every preset is named after the vcpkg triplet it selects, and that triplet ships with vcpkg itself - nothing here carries a triplet file, which is the whole point of the port. An unset VCPKG_BUILD_TYPE builds both Release and Debug, so anything that links Debug gets Debug.

configurePresets.name: x64-windows-static
configurePresets.description: No generator is named on purpose. Naming one would pin one Visual Studio version, and the requirement is Visual Studio 2022 or newer (README, Known limits), not 2022 exactly: left to itself CMake picks the newest Visual Studio installed, so a consumer on 2026 is not forced onto 2022 and one on 2019 fails in the port's build rather than at generator lookup. With no architecture stated either, the target machine type is the machine's own, which is what a Visual Studio generator does by default. CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY has to be stated explicitly: vcpkg's own windows.cmake toolchain sets /MT for building ports, but a consumer's CMake never loads it, so it would default to /MD and fail at link time with LNK2038 against the /MT static library.

configurePresets.name: arm64-windows-static
configurePresets.description: The same settings as the x64 preset, with the arm64 triplet. The machine type follows the machine here as well, so this preset is what CI runs on an arm64 runner rather than a cross build from x64. Node.js 24+ builds Windows arm64 with clang-cl targeting aarch64, which the port sets up itself.

configurePresets.name: x64-osx
configurePresets.description: x86_64 on an arm64 runner: CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES makes the consumer build the same machine type the triplet asks vcpkg for, and vcpkg reads it back to pick the triplet. The binaries the build runs are then x86_64 and need Rosetta 2, which the CI leg provides - a plain arm64 macOS machine does not necessarily have it.
